novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 (thm:sharp-sign-ratio-closure)
novelty_flags.one_line: The flagship-aspirant sharpness claim is a strict comparison only to HuntingtonKlein2026 and is not promoted to a generic class of pairwise-extrema relaxations, so it is capped at field tier.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 (def:gaussian-completion)
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated Gaussian submodel permits correlated observed outcomes or residuals across settings, but the proposed completion independently generates every setting, so its observed margin is generally not P_obs and the load-bearing attainment claim fails on this allowed Gaussian special case.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (thm:sharp-sign-ratio-closure)
soundness_flags.one_line: Its asserted strict comparison refers only to an undefined “symmetric two-setting region”; the required K=2, symmetric-box, and ratio-envelope equalities appear in Theorem 3 but are neither hypotheses nor dependencies of Theorem 1.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 7-9, Assumptions 1-3; p. 13, Proposition 4; pp. 14-15, transitivity remark and Definition 3; pp. 17-18, Assumption 4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the partially linear OVB setting, requires proportional positive ratios with lower bound at most one and upper bound at least one, derives a K-setting pairwise-difference polytope as Proposition 4, defines pinning in Definition 3, and uses divided supershort bias ratios in Assumption 4.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 92(439), 1997
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives sharp, tightest-possible treatment-effect bounds under imperfect compliance, supporting its use only as a general attainment precedent.
The paper develops a random-utility test and an inequality-constraint result using vertices of a polyhedral cone rather than faces; it is a method ancestor rather than an OVB sign-union result.
The article characterizes compatibility using finite inequalities and efficient combinatorial inclusion checks in multiple-equilibrium models.
The paper proposes bootstrap calibrated projection confidence intervals for smooth functions of partially identified parameters in moment (in)equality models and contains a proof of Theorem 3.1.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies 86(1), 2019, version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: With Gaussian first-stage limits, the paper identifies full differentiability as the criterion for ordinary-bootstrap consistency and provides an alternative derivative-based resampling approach for directionally differentiable maps.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 206(2), 2018, version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The numerical delta method gives consistent inference for directionally differentiable maps and uniform validity for specified convex Lipschitz maps under an appropriate step-size sequence.
The paper inverts joint tests to form identification-robust confidence regions for a finite collection of ratios and permits unbounded projected sets.
The paper obtains uniformly correct asymptotic size for conditional tests in a broad class of weak-identification moment models and studies efficiency under strong identification.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2112.13398 public text; cited ReStat version not independently accessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible public text develops sharp single-setting OVB bounds for partially linear and broader causal models and inference for those bounds; it contains no cross-setting multiplicative closure theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the independent-by-setting Gaussian completion with a joint-law-preserving construction, or explicitly restrict the sharpness theorem to a product or suitably jointly Gaussian observed-law family and prove the corresponding completion.
Move the symmetric K=2, box, and ratio-envelope hypotheses into Theorem 1 as a named corollary or make its strictness clause explicitly depend on Theorem 3.

To seek flagship tier, compare against at least one further published common-witness or multi-setting sensitivity relaxation, or prove strictness for a clearly defined generic class of pairwise-extrema outer relaxations.
